title: Tools for Surface Treatment of Silicon Planar Intracortical Microelectrodes
protocol: Assemble the apparatus for handling and holding devices during gas-phase deposition.
Place the devices into the assembled apparatus according to steps 1.1-1.8.
Fasten pieces 1A and 2B together using screws and wing nuts.
Acquire 1 cm x 1 cm square samples of the devices' substrate material.
Cut the silicon wafer into 1 cm x 1 cm squares using a wafer dicing machine.
Print or acquire pieces 1A and 1B.
Attach double-sided polyimide tape to piece 1A.
Attach 1/8" thick foam strip with one-side adhesive to piece 1B.
Adhere the connector packaging of the device to the tape on piece 1A.
Secure piece 1A and piece 1B together using stainless steel screws and wing nuts.
Fasten the assembly to the vacuum desiccator tray using zip ties through the holes in the bottom of piece 1A.
Place square material samples into the slits at the bottom of the frame if applicable.
Position a receptacle with the solution within the vacuum desiccator opposite and in line with the secured assembly.
Place a vacuum gauge within the desiccator to record the exact pressure.
Position the port of the desiccator lid near the secured assembly and in line with the solution.
Assemble the 3D printed guide piece and attach it to the lid of the culture plate.
Stabilize pieces C and D using the benchtop piece during assembly.
Secure the suspension of devices for placement in the well plate by combining pieces C and D.
Further secure pieces C and D to the well plate lid with double-sided polyimide tape on the lower portion of C, and foam tape on the lower portion of D.
Construct a lid for the well plate to suspend the electrode array of the device in solution.
Cut rectangular holes 19 mm x 10.5 mm into the lid of the well plate using a laser cutter or manually with a box cutter.
Match the number of holes to the number of devices desired for treatment.
Print or acquire the appropriate number of guides (piece 2A).
Use cyanoacrylate adhesive to secure guides to the lid.
Align the rectangular holes in the guides and lids while gluing.
Fill the well plate with the desired solution at locations where treatment will occur.
Securely suspend the devices in a well plate.
Tape piece 2B to a benchtop.
Place double-sided polyimide tape to cover the base of piece 2C.
Place 1/8" foam tape with single-side adhesive to cover the base of piece 2D.
Fit piece 2C into the groove of piece 2B.
Adhere the connector packaging of the device onto the tape, oriented so the length of the device shank is suspended.
Slide piece 2D into piece 2C to secure the device between the tool pieces.
Lift the assembly from piece 2A by holding the edges.
Fit the assembly into the lid by aligning the outward-facing semicircles on pieces 2C and 2D with the corresponding guides on piece 2A.
Press-fit piece 2E over the guides to secure assembly placement.
Agitate the well plate for reactions that benefit from continuous mixing of the solution.
Transfer the assembled well plate to a shaker table and run at speeds under 100 rpm.
Carefully transfer the lid to a new well plate with desired solutions distributed to appropriate wells if multiple solution-based reactions or wash steps are required.
Remove devices from the well plate.
Tape piece 2B to a benchtop.
Remove piece 2E from the lid.
Carefully remove the assembly holding the device from the well plate.
Orient the assembly so that piece 2C faces the benchtop and piece 2D faces upward.
Ensure the shank of the device is parallel to the benchtop.
Fit piece 2C into piece 2B as previously completed.
Separate piece 2D from piece 2C by pulling them apart carefully.
Apply slight pressure on the tabs of piece 2C onto the bench for stability.
Use forceps to hold the device's connector packaging.
Remove the device from the tape and transfer it to the desired storage container.
